title: Frontend: Lucky Number
businessContext: Build and verify the core behavior behind Lucky Number. This independently authored exercise has a bounded, explicit contract. Injected clock, network, random, or worker models are identified in the contract; they do not claim production service guarantees.
problemStatement: Export App. From a nonempty Name, compute an entertainment-only deterministic number 1..9: sum Unicode code points of trimmed lowercase text, then sum modulo 9 plus 1. Reject blank with Name required. This is not a predictive claim. Render controlled labelled inputs with these exact names: Name. A Calculate submit button computes the result. Render JSON.stringify(result) in [data-testid="result"]. Validation failure clears result and shows the documented message in [data-testid="error"].
constraints: Export default App. Only react and react/jsx-runtime imports are supported. The DOM contract and supplied props define the exercise.
Preserve identity, ordering, boundary behavior, and error messages stated in the contract. Passing fixtures verifies this contract, not every production concern.
candidateTasks: Implement the documented behavior without hard-coding fixture answers.
Run the full suite, investigate boundary failures, and explain the follow-up variation.
hints: Write down the state or algorithmic invariant, and trace the smallest boundary case before coding.
Define the range, validate any user seed inputs, and generate the result in the action handler.
alternativeApproaches: Offer a seeded reproducible mode and explain its predictability compared with random sampling.
commonMistakes: Ignoring contract boundaries such as: Range endpoints; rerender; repeated reroll.
Treating a local deterministic model as proof of durable storage, authorization, distributed coordination, or physical-world guarantees.
